pure-announcement.rationale: It is a tutorial explaining a prompting technique; no product launch, release, or funding content is present beyond course self-promotion asides.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (Cypher querying, Code Mode, LLM-maintained wiki, retrieval composition, context layer) cover chain-of-thought prompting or its mechanism.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Although it cites no papers, every central claim is directly reproducible by running the given prompts, and the technique is extensively documented in primary literature.

durability.rationale: It explains the mechanism — autoregressive generation lets written-out steps condition later tokens, so decomposition beats one-shot answers on multi-step problems — with no version numbers, and even flags that reasoning models now internalise the same behaviour.

actionability.rationale: A reader leaves with a directly applicable practice: trigger reasoning zero-shot with a step-by-step instruction or few-shot with worked examples, apply it only to multi-step problems, and verify the steps rather than trusting them.

atomicity.rationale: The whole piece states one idea — elicit intermediate reasoning before the answer — and the zero-shot/few-shot variants are modes of that single technique, not separable concepts.
